questions.questionText:
Glider X of mass 400 g travels at 1.8 m s−1 to the right on a horizontal, frictionless track.
Glider Y of mass 300 g travels towards X at 0.7 m s−1.
[diagram needed]
X and Y collide.
Immediately after the collision, Y travels to the right at a speed of 0.9 m s−1.
What are the speed and direction of movement of X immediately after the collision?

media.alt: Diagram of glider X and glider Y travelling on a frictionless track.

questions.explanation: Take right as positive and apply conservation of momentum before and after the collision.

questions.questionText:
A railway truck of mass 8000 kg travels along a level track at a velocity of 2.5 ms–1 and collides with a stationary truck of mass 12000 kg. The two trucks move together at the same velocity after the collision.
[diagram needed]
What is the change in momentum of the 8000 kg truck due to the impact?

media.alt: Diagram of an 8000 kg railway truck moving towards a stationary 12000 kg truck.

questions.explanation: Use conservation of momentum to find the common final velocity, then calculate the 8000 kg truck's change in momentum.

questions.questionText:
An object of mass 0.20 kg moves with an initial velocity u. It collides with a stationary object of mass 0.30 kg.
The objects stick together when they collide.
No external forces act on the objects.
What is the final velocity of the two objects after the collision?
questions.explanation: The objects stick together, so the initial momentum of the 0.20 kg object is shared by the combined 0.50 kg mass.

questions.questionText:
A railway truck of mass 2000 kg travelling horizontally at 1.5 m s–1 collides with a stationary truck of mass 3000 kg.
After the collision they move together.
Which row is correct?

options.A: Speed of the trucks immediately after collision: 0.6 m s–1; effect of collision on total kinetic energy: no change
options.B: Speed of the trucks immediately after collision: 0.6 m s–1; effect of collision on total kinetic energy: decrease
options.C: Speed of the trucks immediately after collision: 1.0 m s–1; effect of collision on total kinetic energy: no change
options.D: Speed of the trucks immediately after collision: 1.0 m s–1; effect of collision on total kinetic energy: decrease

questions.explanation: Momentum is conserved to find the shared speed; because the trucks join, the collision is inelastic and total kinetic energy decreases.

questions.fullQuestionText:
The diagram shows two railway trucks A and B travelling towards each other on the same railway line which is straight and horizontal.
[diagram needed]
The trucks are involved in an inelastic collision. They join when they collide and then move together.
The trucks move a distance of 15 m before coming to rest.
Truck A has a total mass of 16 000 kg and truck B has a total mass of 12 000 kg
Just before the collision, truck A was moving at a speed of 2.8 m s–1 and truck B was moving at a speed of 3.1 m s–1
(a) State the quantity that is not conserved in an inelastic collision.
(b) Show that the speed of the joined trucks immediately after the collision is about 0.3 m s–1
(c) Calculate the impulse that acts on each truck during the collision. Give an appropriate unit for your answer.
(d) Explain, without doing a calculation, how the motion of the trucks immediately after the collision would be different for a collision that is perfectly elastic.

media.alt: Diagram of railway trucks A and B travelling towards each other.

subparts.questionText: State the quantity that is not conserved in an inelastic collision.
Show that the speed of the joined trucks immediately after the collision is about 0.3 m s–1.
markSchemePoints: Attempt to apply conservation of momentum.
16 000 x 2.8 - 12 000 x 3.1 = 28 000 v; substitution must be seen.
v = 0.27(1) m s–1. Correct equation, with signs watched, gets the first and second marks.

subparts.questionText: Calculate the impulse that acts on each truck during the collision. Give an appropriate unit for your answer.
markSchemePoints: Unit: N s or kg m s–1.

subparts.questionText: Explain, without doing a calculation, how the motion of the trucks immediately after the collision would be different for a collision that is perfectly elastic.
markSchemePoints: Velocity of B is greater than that of A because total momentum is to the right, or B has lower mass. Alternative: momentum of B after collision is same as that of A before the collision and vice versa.
